importance_ranking.reason: Tensile structure design is a visually-driven purchase — buyers scan images to confirm the structure type (hypar, conical, barrel vault, canopy), aesthetic quality, and finish before reading any text. High visual variation across sub-types means wrong image = immediate skip; a car parking canopy buyer will not engage with a stadium roof listing.

Buyers shortlist providers based on membrane material (PVC vs PTFE vs PVDF), structure type, and service scope (design-only vs turnkey) before contacting — these specs determine technical fit and budget tier. Without visible specs, buyers cannot determine whether the provider can deliver their specific project requirement.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand with buyer recall exists in this fragmented market — buyers search by capability, portfolio, and geography rather than by company name.
importance_ranking.reason: For a high-value, project-based service, buyers evaluate provider track record, portfolio of completed projects, certifications (IS code compliance, structural engineering credentials), and geographic service reach during vendor shortlisting — company signals matter but rank below visual and spec fit.

Every tensile structure project is custom-quoted per sq ft based on membrane material, structure complexity, area, and site conditions — no fixed list price exists and final pricing is always negotiated. Indian buyers are price-sensitive but cannot compare prices meaningfully across listings without spec equivalence; price is a budget-entry sanity check, not a primary shortlisting signal.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large institutional/stadium projects may quote per sq mt or lump-sum; small bespoke entry canopies may quote per project — but per sq ft is the dominant unit across the Indian market and must be shown to enable any price comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per sq mt vs per project creates real price comparison confusion in this category — buyers cannot interpret or compare any quoted price without knowing the unit basis, making unit display essential alongside any price indication.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Membrane material (PVC vs PTFE vs PVDF vs HDPE) is the single largest price driver in tensile structure projects — PTFE commands a 3–5x premium over PVC and is non-interchangeable for fire-rated or long-lifespan applications, making it the primary product-class separator.

Structure geometry (hypar, conical, barrel vault, canopy, skylight) determines fabrication complexity, steel framework design, and engineering effort — a hypar or conical form requires significantly more design and fabrication cost than a flat canopy, and buyers cannot substitute one form for another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers evaluating PVC vs PTFE vs PVDF membranes make purchase decisions heavily on expected service life (10–15 years vs 30–35 years) and warranty terms — this is a primary differentiator between material tiers that is absent from the current spec list.

Government, institutional, and hospitality buyers (PWD, CPWD, hotels, malls) require fire-rated membranes (Class B1 or Class A / non-combustible PTFE) as a compliance prerequisite — absence of this spec forces buyers to contact every provider individually to confirm eligibility.

Buyers with fixed inauguration dates, event deadlines, or construction schedules use delivery timeline as a hard shortlisting criterion — providers who cannot commit to a timeline are eliminated before contact.
